boeCandidates.fiscalStance: Experienced with Clifton's school budget process from his 2018–2021 tenure on the board; advocates for curbing out-of-district tuition and legal costs by building stronger in-district special education programs and fighting for Clifton's fair share of state aid.
boeCandidates.infrastructureStance: Supports systematic capital planning across Clifton's 17 school buildings, classroom technology modernization, and resolving overcrowding in neighborhood elementary schools.

interviewStances.interviewSource: Passaic County Clerk Certified Filing, Clifton Times Archives & BOE Records
interviewStances.keyPriorities: Former Clifton BOE Commissioner (2018–2021) and credentialed Special Education teacher (M.A., Montclair State); brings immediate board experience and classroom perspective to the 1-year unexpired seat.
interviewStances.facilitiesAndBudget: Focuses on strengthening in-district special education services to improve student outcomes while controlling costly out-of-district placements and administrative overhead.
interviewStances.keyInterviewQuote: With a 1-year unexpired term, there is no time for a learning curve. As a former Clifton BOE Commissioner and Special Education teacher, I am ready to serve our students and taxpayers on Day One.

ballotArchitecture.summary: Registered Clifton voters will vote across four levels of government: Municipal (City Council), School District (Board of Education), County (Passaic County Commissioners & Surrogate), and Federal (U.S. Senate & U.S. House NJ-09).

offices.description: Controls the $105.4M municipal budget, police & fire departments, DPW, zoning, and municipal ordinances. Under Clifton's 1923 Municipal Manager Act, the top vote-getter traditionally serves as Mayor.

offices.voteRule: Full Term: Vote for 3 (of 4) • Unexpired: Vote for 1 (of 2)
offices.description: Oversees 17 public schools, ~11,000 students, and the $293.4M Clifton Public Schools budget. Four candidates (Canova, Suarez, Estrict-Barnes, Siano) are competing for 3 full three-year seats, and two candidates (Lemus, Kasper) are competing for 1 one-year unexpired seat.

Governs Passaic County government, allocating the ~$500M county budget. Maintains county roads in Clifton (Valley Rd, Van Houten Ave, Clifton Ave, Broad St), Passaic County Community College, and county park systems.
Fills an unexpired term on the 7-member Board of County Commissioners through December 31, 2027.

offices.taxShare: Funded via Passaic County General Fund
offices.description: Constitutional Officer serving as Judge of the Surrogate's Court. Manages wills, probate, estates, guardianships, and adoptions across Passaic County.

offices.office: United States Senate (New Jersey, Class II)
offices.description: Represents all New Jerseyans in the U.S. Senate. Four candidates appear on the Clifton ballot: Justin Murphy (R - 1A), Cory Booker (D - 1B), Veronica Fernandez (End The Corruption! - 1C), and Joanne Kuniansky (Socialist Workers Party - 1D).

Represents Clifton, Passaic, Paterson, and Bergen/Hudson portions in Congress. Three candidates appear on the Clifton ballot: Rosie Pino (R - 2A), Nelida Pou (D - 2B), and Terrisa Bukovinac (Save Our Babies - 2C).

usSenate.office: United States Senate (New Jersey, Class II)
usSenate.importance: Represents 9.3M New Jerseyans in Washington D.C. Key powers include confirming federal judges, voting on federal budgets, and fighting for New Jersey's fair share of federal tax returns and SALT deductions.

candidates.name: Justin Murphy (Ballot 1A)
candidates.role: GOP Nominee for U.S. Senate; attorney, former Tabernacle Deputy Mayor and township committeeman.
candidates.keyPriorities: Federal fiscal restraint to curb inflation; national border security; lowering federal middle-class and small-business income tax brackets; full federal SALT relief for suburban homeowners; domestic energy independence.
candidates.localImpact: Pledging to eliminate federal regulatory hurdles delaying North Jersey flood wall infrastructure projects and lower federal cost burdens on New Jersey taxpayers.

candidates.name: Cory Booker (Ballot 1B)
candidates.role: U.S. Senator from New Jersey (in office since 2013); former Mayor of Newark.
candidates.keyPriorities: Restoring full federal State and Local Tax (SALT) deduction ($10K cap repeal); funding Gateway Tunnel & NJ Transit; securing federal clean water grants for Passaic Valley Water Commission (PVWC); prescription drug cost caps.
candidates.localImpact: Secured federal appropriations for Passaic River flood mitigation and lead water pipe replacement projects directly serving Clifton residents.

candidates.name: Veronica Fernandez (Ballot 1C)
candidates.role: Independent U.S. Senate candidate running on the 'End The Corruption!' ballot line.
candidates.keyPriorities: Anti-corruption campaign finance reform, federal government accountability, term limits, and reducing cost-of-living burdens on working families.

candidates.name: Joanne Kuniansky (Ballot 1D)
candidates.role: U.S. Senate candidate running on the 'Socialist Workers Party' ballot line.
candidates.keyPriorities: Trade union solidarity, cost-of-living wage protections, universal healthcare, and working-class labor advocacy.

usHouse.office: U.S. House of Representatives (New Jersey's 9th Congressional District — NJ-09)
usHouse.importance: Clifton is located entirely within New Jersey's 9th Congressional District. The district encompasses Passaic County (Clifton, Passaic, Paterson), southern Bergen County (Hackensack, Fort Lee, Teaneck, Englewood), and Secaucus in Hudson County.

candidates.name: Rosie Pino (Ballot 2A)
candidates.role: GOP Nominee for NJ-09; current Clifton City Councilwoman (first elected 2018) and former Clifton Board of Education Commissioner (2013–2018). Born to immigrant parents, former U.S. Treasury bank examiner, finance professional. Note: Running concurrently for Congress (2A) and for re-election to Clifton City Council (19E).
candidates.keyPriorities: Cutting federal spending and regulatory red tape; small business tax relief; revitalizing commercial and industrial corridors along Route 3 and Route 46; supporting local law enforcement with federal Byrne JAG grants; parent choice in education.
candidates.localImpact: Lifelong advocate for Clifton homeowners on municipal tax relief, flood basin maintenance, and opposing regional congestion pricing models.

candidates.name: Nelida (Nellie) Pou (Ballot 2B)
candidates.role: U.S. Representative (NJ-09). Longtime NJ State Senator (District 35) and former Assemblywoman; succeeded late Congressman Bill Pascrell Jr. in 2024.
candidates.keyPriorities: Securing federal Army Corps of Engineers funding for Passaic River Basin and Third River flood barriers; federal Community Project Funding (earmarks) for Clifton Police & Fire communications; full SALT deduction repeal; expanding federal community health center grants.
candidates.localImpact: Spearheaded state and federal funding for Route 46 and Route 3 highway bottleneck improvements in Clifton and Passaic County.

candidates.name: Terrisa Bukovinac (Ballot 2C)
candidates.role: Independent NJ-09 congressional candidate running on the 'Save Our Babies' ballot line.
candidates.keyPriorities: Anti-abortion advocacy, human rights campaigns, and independent grassroots activism.

passaicCountyCommissionersFull.office: Passaic County Board of County Commissioners (Full 3-Year Terms)
passaicCountyCommissionersFull.importance: The 7-member Board of County Commissioners sets the county tax rate ($0.749 per $100, or 22.92% of your property tax bill). They manage the ~$500M county budget, county roads in Clifton (Valley Rd, Van Houten Ave, Clifton Ave, Broad St), Passaic County Community College, and Passaic County Technical-Vocational Schools (PCTVS).

candidates.slate: Democratic Commissioner Slate (Vote for up to 2)
candidates.keyPriorities: Maintaining Passaic County's strong AA bond credit rating; major county road paving and stormwater culvert modernizations in Clifton (Van Houten Ave, Valley Rd, Clifton Ave); funding PCTVS career/vocational programs; expanding county senior transit and meals-on-wheels; preserving county open space at Garret Mountain and Weasel Brook Park in Clifton.

candidates.slate: Republican Commissioner Slate (Vote for up to 2)
candidates.keyPriorities: Enacting a county property tax freeze; commissioning an independent forensic audit of all Passaic County departmental spending and vendor contracts; eliminating political patronage positions; prioritizing county stormwater infrastructure dollars for flood-prone neighborhoods in Clifton.

passaicCountyCommissionersUnexpired.office: Passaic County Board of County Commissioners (1-Year Unexpired Term)
passaicCountyCommissionersUnexpired.importance: Fills an unexpired vacancy on the Passaic County Board of County Commissioners for the remainder of the calendar year.

candidates.name: Aleksandra Tasic
candidates.role: Public policy advocate and civic leader.
candidates.keyPriorities: Transparent county budgeting, expanding youth recreation and mental health counseling services, and upgrading county parks.

candidates.name: Marko Kopic
candidates.role: Small business owner and fiscal watchdog.
candidates.keyPriorities: Holding the line on county property taxes, eliminating wasteful spending, and improving county public works efficiency.

passaicCountySurrogate.importance: Constitutional Officer serving as Judge of the Surrogate's Court. Manages the probate of wills, administration of intestate estates, legal guardianships for minors and incapacitated adults, and adoption records across Passaic County.

candidates.name: Zoila Cassanova
candidates.role: Passaic County Surrogate (serving since 2021); attorney with extensive estate and probate litigation background.
candidates.keyPriorities: Expanding community outreach seminars in multiple languages across Clifton to educate seniors and families on wills and estates; expanding digital court filings; safeguarding protected assets for vulnerable residents.

candidates.name: Jessica Sprague
candidates.role: Attorney and municipal prosecutor with deep estate law and family litigation experience.
candidates.keyPriorities: Modernizing Surrogate's Court operations to eliminate probate delays for grieving families; expanding evening and satellite hours in Clifton and suburban towns; enhancing public transparency.
